description: Crystal Lake Dam lake-rise model. Parameters from the Hydrologic Reference (June 2026): Dinicola 1990 Till Forest HSPF set + 2007 HEC-HMS geometry. US customary units throughout (inches, cfs, acres, acre-feet, feet, hours).

watershed.deep_loss_comment: Small constant deep-groundwater loss applied to bucket overflow before interflow. NOT the doc's 27% total loss: that 27% is 'split between deep groundwater AND retained soil storage' (Reference 1.9), and soil retention is already captured by the SM bucket here. Calibrated so the Step 6 saturated anchor peaks at ~343.1 ft (the prediction target). CALIBRATION FOLLOW-UP: the slow IRC interflow routing attenuates the instantaneous peak inflow (~285 vs HEC-HMS 884 cfs) even though peak elevation matches via volume; revisit once a real storm is logged.

datum.comment: Maps the HA lake-depth sensor reading to absolute elevation: abs = reading + sensor_to_absolute_offset_ft. PROVISIONAL (open item #2): the doc's +339.0 is the staff/WQ frame, but sensor.crystal_lake_depth has a DIFFERENT zero. 338.375 is cross-checked from the existing HA helper crystal_lake_threshold_summer_normal=1.3 (depth) corresponding to the doc's 3-log summer pool 339.675 ft (i.e. 339.675-1.3). Independently corroborated: a hindcast from the June seasonal default lands at ~339.68 ft for the current 1.36 reading. CONFIRM with a field tape-down before trusting absolute thresholds.

leakage.comment: cfs is the modeled constant seepage through the stop-logs near the control elevation; cfs_low/high is the documented un-calibrated range (Reference 4.4a). cfs=0.8 keeps the 72 h dry-recession anchor within the observed 339.6-339.8 ft quasi-equilibrium band. Needs field calibration from a real dry spell.

seasonal_sm_default_frac_of_lzsn.comment: Fraction of LZSN to seed SM by month when insufficient rainfall history exists for replay (Reference 1.5). Dry late-summer -> near 0; near-saturated Dec-Apr -> ~1.0.

uncertainty.comment: Manufactured scenario band (HA exposes no percentiles, spec 4.7). Multipliers on median precip for low/high; band widens with lead time.
